ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.74 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexcused detour on the 09:47–09:53 segment; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file (no account flag, no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the only chat message [F7] is a pickup arrangement (kerb outside Mandarin Gallery, red jacket) — not a threat. The driver's statement [F9] is a factual denial, not abuse. The complaint contains no safety or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none; no escalation on SAFE grounds.

Evidence: the record settles every element needed — GPS actual vs optimal distance [F1], one off-route segment with its duration, distance and extra km [F3], the fare breakdown, metered distance and per-km distance fare [F4][F6]. Nothing is missing or untimestamped [F7][F8]. evidence_status = sufficient.

Route deviation: RydeTAXI, so RD-2's metered branch applies — extra distance enters the meter. Segment [F3] 09:47–09:53 is an off-route segment: 3.83 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.89 km, +1.94 km, up to 777 m off the optimal route — well beyond the 0.2 km matching-noise layer, so RD-1 is engaged.

Exemptions examined and rejected:
• RD-3 — no rider-named stop and no in-app destination edit; the sole chat message [F7] is a pickup point at the origin, not a mid-trip stop, so no segment is exempted on that basis.
• RD-5 — there is no consent message from the rider at all (1 message, [F7][F8]), and a driver's untested "my GPS rerouted me" claim [F9] is a statement, not consent, and cannot stand in for the rider's own message. No general or named-road authorisation exists. Finding: counts.
• RD-4 — no reasonable-cause exemption: [F12] records no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window. The speed-band facts [F10][F11] show band 4 (30–39 km/h), not band 1 or 2, and in any case a band fact alone does not exempt a segment (RD-4(b)); the banded roads also are not tied to the replaced portion of the optimal route. Not exempted.

Amount (RD-2, metered formula): the unexcused segment's extra_km = 1.94 km × this trip's per-km rate. Per-km rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $18.50 ÷ 13.12 km = $1.4101/km [F4][F6]. 1.94 × 1.4101 = $2.736 → $2.74. Note the billed excess is only $3.44 for 2.44 km [F4]; the 0.50 km difference beyond the segment (route-corridor/matching slippage not attributed to any segment) is not refunded under RD-2. Stop/waiting time is $0.00 [F6], so nothing to return there. ruling = refund_partial, $2.74.

Account flag: RD-6 requires, in addition to an upheld breach in this case, `route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1`. The driver profile [F15] shows 1 upheld dispute but route: 0, and the rider profile [F14] shows 0 upheld — the threshold is not met. flag_account = false; record the RD-1 breach only.

segment_findings.reason: 09:47–09:53 off-route segment, +1.94 km, up to 777 m from the optimal route. No rider-named place or stop (RD-3 fails: the only rider message [F7] fixes the pickup kerb, not a mid-trip stop). No consent: there is no rider message authorising any route change — the record holds one timestamped rider message only [F7][F8], and the driver's post-trip 'my GPS rerouted me' statement [F9] is a claim, not consent (RD-5). No reasonable cause: no traffic incident near the route in the trip window [F12], and band 4 speeds [F10][F11] are neither band 1 nor 2 and do not tie to the replaced portion (RD-4). Unexempted under RD-1; refund under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's claim that GPS rerouting excuses the deviation: a route must still be the shortest and most direct absent reasonable cause (RD-1), and no traffic incident corroborates a re-route ([F12]; band 4 in [F10][F11] is not band 1/2 and is not tied to the replaced road). A driver statement also cannot substitute for the rider's own consent message (RD-5).
No rider message names a place, approves a route, or requests a stop; the single chat message [F7] concerns the pickup point, so no segment is exempted under RD-3 or RD-5.

RD-2 refunds only the unexcused segment's extra_km (1.94 km, $2.74). The residual 0.50 km in the billed excess [F4] (corridor back-and-forth, map-matching slippage) is not attributed to any segment and is not refunded.
RD-6 needs a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days plus this case; the driver profile [F15] shows 1 upheld dispute but route: 0, so the repeated-violation threshold is not met.
